t: 37 laws of power of the gray man

b.x: Craft, not a court

These are the 37 laws of power of the gray man — and of the survivalist who does not want to become a poster. It is nobody's book. Not a court, not a militia, not how to rule. It is what Tuesday asks when the street tightens: shadow, a quiet stock, water, law, a low pulse. Power, here, is margin: not being picked, not being mapped, not kneeling on the stage.

Gray man and survivalist are the same craft at two speeds. One crosses the street without being the portrait. The other holds the house when the tap, the pole, or the till fail. Without the first, the second becomes a target. Without the second, the first is only style. The 37 bind both: wear the street, keep the stock, read the ask, refuse stage fear, obey the law.
DON'T
Do not use this as a sword. Do not manipulate, blackmail, or build a militia. Defense. If the scene wounds: emergency services. The local law, not the forum's law.
01–07 · Shadow and street

01 01. Wear the street. A gray man does not wear the hobby. Wear the block you are on: colour, cut, shoe, volume. The survivalist in a tactical shirt at the grocer has already chosen to be the poster.

02 02. Speak less than necessary. The street and the crisis pay whoever explains too much. One sentence, one fact, one number. The rest is a map you hand over for free. A talkative survivalist becomes a walking inventory.

03 03. Do not announce the stock. Pantry, generator, route, point B: that does not go to the group, the story, the lobby. Whoever knows what you have, in a blackout, chooses the door. Gray keeps it. The survivalist who posts a shelf is asking for a visit.

04 04. Be hard to describe. Gray is not invisible: boring on purpose. After the street, nobody can close the portrait — not colour, not brand, not cut. The survivalist who fits an identikit has already lost the margin.

05 05. Three layers must match. Look, pace, information. Tuesday clothes with an operator's step and a bunker mouth do not stick. The eye reads the mismatch before the sentence. Wear, walk, and speak the same block.

06 06. Read the ask under the talk. The talk wants one thing; the mouth says another. Gray asks: what does this sentence gain if I say yes? In chaos, the polite ask maps kit, route, home. Answer what was said. Keep the rest.

07 07. Too sweet has already chosen the target. Flattery, a rush to help, trust me. In disaster that arrives early. Gray thanks them, does not open the door, does not show the stock. The survivalist who needs to be liked pays in information.
08–14 · Information and order

01 08. Do not fill the silence. Whoever fills it hands over the engine: fear, plan, address. Leave the pause. The other talks. Gray watches. The survivalist who explains the kit in the elevator has already briefed the thief.

02 09. The phone is a witness. The cloud files it. A group is a stage. An online translator reads what you paste. Gray treats the device as a field radio: little, short, no map. In a blackout, what lives only on the phone does not exist.

03 10. One ear on the street. One earbud only. Screen off the crosswalk. The second ear belongs to the sidewalk, the engine, the shout. Situational awareness is not an app: it is the body in the room. Whoever crosses the avenue in the feed has already donated Tuesday.

04 11. No photo of the kit. Molle, a patch, a generator, a shelf, my bug-out. The image travels farther than you. Gray does not become a catalogue. The survivalist who needs a like on the gear has already lost the craft.

05 12. Dry papers beat a gadget. ID, prescription, an out-of-city contact, insurance — a dry copy, a bag, a folder. Gadgets get wet, die, vanish. Gray and survivalist: boring paper opens a door when the screen will not light.

06 13. Water first, opinion later. Three to four litres per person per day. Boil, filter, tap bleach in the right dose. The collapse debate does not drink. A survivalist with opinions and no water has a stage.

07 14. The rule of threes runs the panic. Air, shelter, water, food, hope, security — in that order. Under pressure the head wants to jump to the weapon, the generator, the theory. Gray returns to the order. Whoever inverts the list dies of a cheap thing.
15–21 · House and margin

01 15. A pantry of what the house already eats. Rice, beans, tins, oats — Tuesday's plate, in volume. Forum food nobody in the house will eat becomes expensive trash. A survivalist feeds people, not the ego of the shelf.

02 16. Turn the stock. FIFO: what comes in at the back, what leaves at the front. A date on the tin, an eye on weevils. Humidity, pests, and dates eat more stock than the blackout. Gray treats the pantry as craft, not an altar.

03 17. A fourteen-day island. Water, food, light, medicine, hygiene for two weeks without a queue. Not a bunker. Margin for flood, strike, fever, price. Whoever already has fourteen days does not join the first supermarket panic.

04 18. Point B on paper. Where the family meets if the house fails. Route A and C. A written stay-or-leave rule. We'll figure it out is not a plan. Gray agrees it on a Tuesday. A survivalist without point B has only a wish.

05 19. A boring 72-hour bag. Water, food, light, radio, papers, medicine, hygiene, one note. Light, no stage, at the door. Not a jungle fantasy. It is the Tuesday the building evacuates and you do not argue about what to take.

06 20. EDC without a stage. In the pocket: ID, cash, light, keys, one note. No molle, no patch, no shop-window knife. The survivalist who dyes the operator belt at the bakery has already described himself.

07 21. First aid before the jungle. A live course, a real pharmacy, wound, burn, faint. Dengue and leptospirosis after a flood matter more than the machete. Gray trains the house's body. Hunting fantasy can wait.
22–28 · People and pulse

01 22. One real neighbour, not a militia. The lone wolf is a film myth. One person in the building who swaps flour and a note. No lobby group, no uniform, no us against them. A short net. The law on the tongue.

02 23. Refuse stage urgency. Now or you lose it, last one run, a headline that tightens the chest. Fear is a product. Gray leaves, drinks water, reads three facts. The survivalist who buys in fright fills the house with trash and debt.

03 24. A cluster, not one signal. One smile, one tremor, one sweet sentence — alone it proves nothing. Three signals in the same direction, in the same minute, in the same body. Gray waits for the cluster. An early conclusion is a stage.

04 25. Fear does not govern. Fear lowers frequency, narrows vision, co-creates the worst Tuesday. Media, pulpit, and group sell a high pulse. Gray names the fear, does not obey it. A paranoid survivalist spends the stock before the crisis.

05 26. Refuse the pulpit and the headline. Whoever shouts wake up also wants a knee. Church, channel, leader, pastor, influencer: intent matters more than volume. Gray reads the line underneath. Do not swap one dogma for another in a different uniform.

06 27. Know if you freeze. Self-knowledge first. Under pressure some run, some shout, some lock. Training on the easy shows the engine. Gray does not fake courage. The survivalist who does not know himself chooses badly in the first hour.

07 28. Ego in the pocket. Whoever needs to be right about collapse becomes a poster. Whoever needs to be the most prepared in the group has already announced the stock. Gray runs the plan and stays quiet. The craft is not identity; it is margin for the family.
29–37 · Law, drill, refusal

01 29. The local law rules. Emergency numbers on the tongue. Ambulance, Civil Defense, the local number. This guide is educational. It does not replace a doctor, a lawyer, a live course. Gray obeys the law. Militia fantasy is a stage and, in Brazil, a crime.

02 30. Weapons only inside the law. This notebook does not teach use, calibre, or a recipe. Where the law allows, the law rules — licence, storage, a course. Where it does not allow, do not invent one. Gray and survivalist: a fight avoided is worth more than a chest.

03 31. Train on the easy. One night without power on purpose. Water boiled on a Saturday. The bag at the door, a clock. The body learns when it does not hurt. The survivalist who only reads forums arrives raw at the flood.

04 32. Hope is margin. The rule of threes includes hope: a why for the family, a note, a point B. Without that the plan dies on the first night. Gray does not farm panic. A survivalist with no what-for becomes paranoia with a pantry.

05 33. Watch more than you conclude. Eye, ear, cluster. An early conclusion feeds the ego and misses the room. Gray notes what he saw, not what he already knows. In chaos, the rush to name it is the trap.

06 34. Do not swap herds. Leaving one dogma for another uniform is still a herd. The awake, a militia, a collapse sect, a channel that hates the street. Gray thinks alone enough not to kneel in the new group.

07 35. Body, sleep, real food. Frequency is not cheap mysticism: it is sleep, water, movement, food the house recognises. Too much industrial food lowers the margin. On a heavy day: carb, protein, good fat. Gray looks after the instrument.

08 36. The family is the system. A one-page plan on the fridge. Child, elder, animal, one real neighbour. The survivalist who prepares only for himself fails in the first hour someone in the house needs him. Gray is not a wolf.

09 37. Refuse the stage of these laws. This is a shield, not a sword. Using the 37 to rule the other is becoming the stage gray refuses. Read, train, be quiet. If the scene wounds: the local law, not the forum's law.
How to use it on a Tuesday

Do not memorise the 37 to recite them. Pick three this week: one of shadow (street, mouth, phone), one of margin (water, pantry, point B), one of pulse (fear, cluster, law). Train on the easy. The clickable list is in Kits. Field 48 (defenses against the stage) is the short shield; this is the full craft — gray and survival in the same notebook.
DO
One law a day, seven days. No photo. No group. Paper on the fridge if the family needs point B. Emergency numbers on the tongue.
NOTE
Educational content. Not a substitute for professional training, medical advice, or local authorities.
